lessons.title: FOR and NEXT
intro: In Unit 2 you built loops by hand: set a counter, increase it, check it with IF, jump back with GOTO. Because loops are needed everywhere, BASIC has a shortcut for exactly that pattern.
FOR I = 1 TO 5 sets I to 1 and marks the start of the loop. NEXT I increases I by 1 and jumps back, until I has passed 5.
Everything between FOR and NEXT is the body of the loop. It runs once for every value of I.

exercises.explanation: The loop runs for I = 1, 2 and 3, and each round prints the current value of I.
NEXT I increases I and jumps back to the start of the loop until I has passed 5.

exercises.prompt: What is the last number this program prints?
exercises.explanation: It prints 1, 4, 9 and 16. The last round has K = 4, and 4 * 4 = 16.

exercises.prompt: This loop can't work. Which line is wrong?
exercises.explanation: NEXT must name the same variable as its FOR. The loop counts with I, so it has to be NEXT I.

exercises.prompt: Compared to the counter loops from Unit 2, what does FOR…NEXT do for you?
options: It sets, increases and checks the counter automatically
It makes the program run backwards
It removes the need for END
It can only count up to 10
exercises.explanation: FOR…NEXT does the LET, the + 1, the IF and the GOTO in just two lines.

exercises.prompt: Build a program that adds up the numbers 1 to 10 and prints 55.
exercises.explanation: S starts at 0, the loop adds every number from 1 to 10, and after the loop the total is printed.

lessons.title: Counting in Steps
intro: By default, FOR counts up by 1. With STEP you choose the step size: FOR I = 2 TO 10 STEP 2 counts 2, 4, 6, 8, 10.
A negative STEP counts down: FOR C = 10 TO 1 STEP -1 is a countdown.
STEP can even be a decimal number, like 0.5.

exercises.prompt: How many numbers does this program print?
exercises.explanation: It prints 0, 5, 10, 15 and 20. That's five numbers.

exercises.prompt: Make it count down from 10 to 1.
exercises.explanation: STEP -1 subtracts 1 every round, so the loop counts down.

exercises.prompt: Which line starts a loop over only the odd numbers from 1 to 9?

exercises.explanation: X starts at 1 and grows by 0.5 each round: 1, 1.5, 2.
In Dartmouth BASIC, NEXT always names its variable: NEXT I.

exercises.prompt: Build a countdown from 5 to 1, followed by LIFTOFF.
exercises.explanation: The loop counts down with STEP -1. Only after the loop has finished does LIFTOFF appear.

lessons.title: Loops inside Loops
intro: A loop can contain another loop. For every single round of the outer loop, the inner loop runs completely.
The inner loop must be closed first: its NEXT comes before the NEXT of the outer loop.
Tip: a semicolon at the end of PRINT keeps printing on the same line, and an empty PRINT starts a new line. That's how you build rows and tables.

exercises.prompt: How many times does line 30 run?
exercises.explanation: The inner loop runs 4 times for each of the 3 outer rounds: 3 × 4 = 12.
I = 1 gives 1+1 and 1+2, then I = 2 gives 2+1 and 2+2: 2, 3, 3, 4.

exercises.prompt: The loops are closed in the wrong order. Which line should come later?
exercises.explanation: The inner loop (J) has to be closed first. It should be NEXT J in line 40 and NEXT I in line 50.

exercises.prompt: Keep all numbers of a row on the same line.
exercises.explanation: A semicolon at the end keeps the cursor on the same line, so the next number continues the row.

exercises.prompt: What does the empty PRINT in line 50 do?
options: It ends the row and starts a new line
exercises.explanation: PRINT without anything just ends the current line. Without it, all numbers would end up in one long row.

exercises.prompt: Build a triangle of stars: one star, then two, then three.
exercises.explanation: The inner loop runs up to R, so row 1 gets one star, row 2 two stars, and row 3 three stars.
